messages.subject: Interpretation of Parameters Fit Through Softmax Link
parts:
This is probably a pretty basic question to someone with experience, but I am struggling with interpreting some parameters. Normally, I would ignore the parameter values and examine predictions, but this time I really need to focus on the parameters themselves.

The model:
############################### Loop over years
 for (y in 1:Y){
############################### Learning Equation
 for(m in 1:(M-1)){
   Alpha[m] <- Theta[p,m,1] +  Theta[p,m,2]*Ifr_local[m,(y-1)] + Theta[p,m,3]*Iwr2_local[m,(y-1)] + Theta[p,m,4]*Sfr[m,(y-1)] + Theta[p,m,5]*Swr[m,(y-1)] + Theta[p,m,6]*Pfr[m,(y-1)] + Theta[p,m,7]*Pwr[m,(y-1)];
              }
   Alpha[M] <- 0;

   I2_local ~ multinomial(softmax(Alpha));
      }

Alpha, is this case, is a vector to be turned into a simplex, and is used to pass information to the probability statement at each pass through the loop.

The Thetas are unique to a category (m), and a person (p). Right now I'm using K-1 vectors, by fixing the last category to zero, prior to running the softmax.

Each kind of data in the model is on the unit interval, so it would be nice if I could compare the importance of each kind of data to the outcome simply by comparing the absolute value of the parameters, both across categories and across data types within a category; however, I'm not sure if this is possible if I fix one category to zero by fiat. So the questions are:

1. What is the interpretation of the Theta parameters as I have written them... What are the units?

2. If I were to use regularizing priors and K vectors instead, what would be the interpretation of the Theta parameters then?

Thanks for the help!

> Each kind of data in the model is on the unit interval, so it would be nice if I could compare the importance of each kind of data to the outcome simply by comparing the absolute value of the parameters, both across categories and across data types within a category; however, I'm not sure if this is possible if I fix one category to zero by fiat. So the questions are:
>
> 1. What is the interpretation of the Theta parameters as I have written them... What are the units?

It helps to look at a binary case and then extend intuitions.
In the binary case, the Alpha are log odds, as in the linear
predictor for a logistic regression. This highlights that the Theta are
just logistic regression coefficients, which is something like change in
log odds per unit of predictor they're being multiplied by. So if the
predictor is height, then it's change in log odds per unit height.

Going beyond binary, the Alpha are still log odds vs. the final outcome, but
this doesn't give you an overall marginal probability, just log odds
vs. the distinguished outcome. But, the theta are still interpretable in
the same units. They're still change in log odds per unit of predictor, only
now it's log odds vs. the distinguished outcome.
> 2. If I were to use regularizing priors and K vectors instead, what would be the interpretation of the Theta parameters then?

The Alpha don't have the same clean interpretation any more, as
they're only interpretable relative to each other. Without the prior,
they're only identified up to adding a constant to each. The theta
are still regression coefficients, though, and still have the same units,
namely change in log odds per unit of predictor.

- Bob
